details:
Lunar AI is an AI-powered web platform designed to support lunar mission planning and decision-making, with a focus on exploring the Moon’s North and South Poles. The platform brings mission planning, lunar data analysis, risk assessment, interactive visualizations, and 3D lunar exploration into one unified environment.

The project works by allowing users to enter mission information such as the destination, mission duration, objectives, and vehicle type. Lunar AI then organizes and analyzes relevant lunar conditions, helping users understand terrain and elevation, sunlight and illumination, water-ice resources, power availability, Earth communication visibility, and landing-site suitability. The results are presented through charts, analysis, maps, and an interactive 3D lunar explorer, making complex scientific information easier to understand.

The main benefit of Lunar AI is that it transforms complex lunar data into clear and accessible insights. It can help users compare potential regions, identify promising landing areas, understand environmental risks, and make more informed mission-planning decisions. Instead of relying on separate tools and large amounts of technical information, users can explore important mission factors within one platform.

The intended impact of the project is to make lunar exploration planning more efficient, understandable, and data-driven. Lunar AI aims to support future exploration by helping students, researchers, engineers, and space enthusiasts visualize lunar conditions and better understand the challenges of operating near the Moon’s polar regions.

The project was developed as a web application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with modern web technologies and libraries for interactive visualizations and 3D exploration. Tools and technologies include Three.js for the 3D lunar environment, Chart.js for charts and data visualization, and JavaScript-based interfaces for mission planning and AI-assisted interactions. NASA lunar datasets and scientific resources were considered as important sources for understanding lunar terrain, illumination, resources, and environmental conditions.

Lunar AI is creative because it combines several traditionally separate aspects of space mission planning into one interactive experience. Instead of presenting lunar information only as tables or technical documents, the project turns it into an interactive environment where users can plan missions, analyze data, explore the Moon in 3D, compare regions, and understand potential risks.

During development, the team considered usability, scientific relevance, visual clarity, accessibility, mission safety, data interpretation, and the complexity of lunar polar environments. The team also considered responsive design, Arabic and English language support, light and dark modes, and the need to make the platform accessible to different types of users. Overall, Lunar AI combines AI, scientific data, visualization, and interactive technology to create a smarter and more accessible approach to lunar mission planning.
